Q1.answer: Ten section 338 documents: (1) Proc. 11046, Doc. 2026-14991, 91 FR 46639, signed 7/20/26, published 7/23/26—50% duty on Annex II Canadian alcoholic beverages; operative from 12:01 a.m. ET 8/22/26 as amended (originally printed 8/19), measured against goods entered for consumption or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption. (2) Proc. 11047, 2026-14992, 91 FR 46653, signed 7/20, published 7/23—same 50% duty on Annex II dairy; same date/event. (3) Proc. 11048, 2026-14997, 91 FR 46663, signed 7/20, published 7/23—same 50% duty on Annex II motor vehicles; same date/event. (4) Proc. 11056, 2026-17294, 91 FR 54789, signed 8/18, published 8/24—3-day suspension; changes effective date to 12:01 a.m. ET 8/22/26, measured against entry/withdrawal; amends Annex II chapeaux and provides refunds. (5) Proc. 11061, 2026-18835, 91 FR 58311, signed 9/8, published 9/14—excludes certain alcoholic beverages from importation from 12:01 a.m. ET 9/29/26, measured against goods imported (physical importation). (6) Proc. 11062, 2026-18836, 91 FR 58319, signed 9/8, published 9/14—same import exclusion for dairy. (7) Proc. 11063, 2026-18837, 91 FR 58325, signed 9/8, published 9/14—same import exclusion for motor vehicles. (8) Proc. 11064, 2026-18838, 91 FR 58331, signed 9/8, published 9/14—alcoholic scope modification: Annex I-A adds, Annex I-B removes; duties apply in addition to §232; from 12:01 a.m. ET 9/15/26, entry/withdrawal. (9) Proc. 11065, 2026-18839, 91 FR 58339, signed 9/8, published 9/14—motor-vehicle scope modification: Annex I-A adds, Annex I-B removes; duties apply in addition to §232; from 12:01 a.m. ET 9/15/26, entry/withdrawal. (10) Proc. 11076, 2026-22292, 91 FR 68861, signed 10/23, filed 10/29, published 10/30—further motor-vehicle scope modification: Annex I-A removes, Annex I-B adds; duties apply in addition to §232; from 12:01 a.m. ET 10/30/26, entry/withdrawal. Product groups: alcoholic—11046 imposed; 11064 changed scope; 11061 converted listed products to an import ban. Dairy—11047 imposed; 11062 converted listed products to a ban; no dairy scope modification was published (11062's reference to one is erroneous). Motor vehicles—11048 imposed; 11065 and 11076 changed scope; 11063 converted listed products to a ban.
Q1.uncertainty: 11046/47/48 operative clauses (1) and (3) still print August 19 because 11056 amended only the Annex II chapeau; later documents contradictorily recite both August 19 and August 22. The operative August 22 date is established by 11056 clause (1) and its supersession clause (5), and confirmed by later recitals.

Q2.answer: (a) Entry 1 (8/20, 2 p.m.): $0. Entry 2 (8/21, 11:59 p.m.): $0. Entry 3 (8/22, 12:01 a.m.): $40,000 × 50% = $20,000. (b) 11046 clauses (1) and (3) print August 19, 2026. Proc. 11056 clause (1) says the effective date of the duties in 11046/47/48 "shall be 12:01 a.m. ... August 22, 2026," and amends only "the chapeau of Annex II" of each proclamation, replacing August 19 with August 22. The operative clauses (1)/(3) were not amended and still print August 19. The later-in-time operative clause (1), plus 11056 clause (5) (inconsistent prior provisions superseded), resolves it in favor of August 22; later proclamations recite that the duties became effective August 22. (c) Proc. 11056 clause (4): refunds "shall be processed pursuant to applicable law and CBP's standard procedures for such refunds"; clause (2) also directed suspension of collection. (d) No further presidential action was needed. Later documents state Canada reneged on August 21, 2026, and that at 12:01 a.m. ET on August 22 the 3-day suspension lapsed and the duties became effective. (e) Section 338 permits duties not to take effect earlier than 30 days after the President's proclamation finding. Signed July 20: July 20-31 = 11 days; August 1-19 = 19 days; 11 + 19 = 30, so August 19 was the earliest permissible date.
Q2.uncertainty: The original clauses (1)/(3) were never formally amended and still print August 19; the documents do not explain this drafting gap.

Q3.answer: (a) A: may be imported; 50% × $30,000 = $15,000. B: may be imported; imported before 9/29 but withdrawn after; 11061 clause (2) preserves the 50% duty = $15,000. C: imported 11:30 p.m. 9/28, before the ban; entered 9/29; clause (2) preserves 50% = $15,000. D: imported 12:30 a.m. 9/29, on/after the ban's effective time—excluded from importation; no duty because inadmissible. (b) E: imported 9/25 before the ban; on 10/6 entry from FTZ, clause (2) applies and the 50% duty is $15,000; it should have been admitted in privileged foreign status. (d) No. 11061 clause (3) says the proclamation does not otherwise affect products subject to 11046 as established by the alcoholic scope modification; non-Annex products remain at 50%.
Q3.uncertainty: The documents do not expressly address entry from an FTZ of goods imported before the ban; clause (2) is the best reading.

Q11.answer: Discrepancies found: (1) In each of 11061, 11062, 11063, 11064, 11065 and 11076, recital 1 says the §338 duties were "effective August 19, 2026," while recital 4 of the same document says they "became effective" at 12:01 a.m. on August 22, 2026 (91 FR 58311, 58319, 58325, 58331, 58339, 68861). (2) 11056 clause (1) states that the effective date "shall be" August 22 and that "accordingly" only "the chapeau of Annex II" is amended, but the operative clauses (1) and (3) of 11046/47/48 still print August 19 (54790 vs. 46641, 46655, 46665). (3) 11062 clause (3) refers to a "Proclamation of September 8, 2026 (Modifying the Scope ... With Respect to Dairy)" that was never issued; no dairy scope modification appears in the Federal Register (58320). (4) 11064/11065/11076 recitals state the §338 30-day waiting period, but their operative clauses make newly listed products dutiable 7 days after signing (58332, 58340, 68862). (5) The §301 memorandum says the June proposal's textile mechanism would allow imports "at a zero section 301 tariff rate" (47719), while the June proposal and the notice say "a reduced Section 301 tariff rate" (34274; 47318). (6) The notice's response-to-comments statement that "many inputs, including auto parts already subject to Section 232 tariffs, are exempt" (47334) is accurate only for the headings enumerated in note 52(f)(3) (47362-63); a §232 heading not listed is not exempt (see Q9(e)).
Q11.uncertainty: Whether item (6) is a true discrepancy or merely imprecise shorthand is arguable; the first five are textual conflicts.

Q14.answer: 1. Incorrect. The memo sets no September 1 deadline; it says USTR advised TRQs were not feasible then but "will be feasible by September 1, 2026," and directs establishment "as soon as the Trade Representative determines that it is feasible" (47720-21). 2. Incorrect. 450 comments/nearly 60 witnesses were the initiation-stage figures (34273); the proposed action drew over 1,600 comments and over 100 witnesses (47319; 47719). 3. Partly correct. Seven economies are named, but Cambodia and Guatemala were already proposed at 10% (ART commitments), and Jordan moved for an ART commitment, not a ban; only Honduras, India, Sri Lanka and Trinidad moved from 12.5% because of bans (47720; 34274; 47324, 47327). 4. Incorrect. USTR determined not to remove beef and avocados; they remain exempt (47331). 5. Incorrect. Japan and Korea are net-of-MFN but have only the general Part A list, not their own negotiated list (47324; Annex II table, 47395). 6. Partly correct. 471 additional products is correct, but only "certain" sugar and sugar-containing products were exempted, not all (47331). 7. Incorrect. The cap limits only EU/Taiwan (10%) and Japan/Korea/Switzerland (12.5%); other economies pay 12.5% on top of MFN, so total can exceed 12.5% (47719-20; 47320-21). 8. Correct (47321; note 52(a)). 9. Correct (memo §4(e), 47722-23; notice 47335). 10. Correct (47330).

Q15.answer: Case N / Case U additional duties (MFN excluded): 1. 2/10/25: $0 / $0. 2. 3/6/25: $25,000 IEEPA / $25,000 IEEPA (USMCA exemption effective 3/7). 3. 3/10/25: $25,000 IEEPA / $0. 4. 3/14/25: $25,000 IEEPA / $25,000 §232 (25%). 5. 6/3/25: $25,000 IEEPA / $25,000 §232 (25%). 6. 6/10/25: $50,000 §232 / $50,000 §232. 7. 8/5/25: $50,000 §232 / $50,000 §232. 8. 3/2/26: $50,000 §232 / $50,000. 9. 6/10/26: $50,000 §232 / $50,000. 10. 7/27/26: $50,000 §232 / $50,000. 11. 8/25/26: $50,000 §232 / $50,000. 12. 9/14/26: $50,000 §232 / $50,000. 13. 9/16/26: $100,000 (§232 $50,000 + §338 $50,000) / same. 14. 11/10/26: $100,000 / same. Why other duties are not owed: IEEPA 25%/35% (EO 14193, as amended by EO 14325) applied until terminated by EO 14389 (2/20/26), but under EO 14289 §3(a)(ii) it was not stacked on §232 after 6/4/25; before that, §232 was not stacked on IEEPA, and USMCA goods were exempt from IEEPA from 3/7/25. Section 232 aluminum: 10% before 3/12/25 but Canada's Proclamations 9893/10106 arrangements remained effective until then; 25% from 3/12/25; 50% from 6/4/25; 50% under Annex I-A from 4/6/26. The §122 surcharge never applied because it was not in addition to §232 and exempted §232 articles, and it expired 7/24/26. Section 301 is exempt under note 52(f)(1) (9903.82.02) and, for Case U, note 52(g). Section 338 applied from 9/15/26 only, because 11048 clause (2) excluded §232 articles before then; 11065/11076 make it cumulative with §232.
Q15.uncertainty: On 2/10/25, if the stipulated "within the section 232 aluminum duties" assumption is read to override the Canada alternative agreements, the 10% rate under Proclamation 9704 would yield $10,000; the Register text shows the Canada arrangements still effective until 3/12/25, so the primary answer is $0. The exact date IEEPA collection ceased after EO 14389 is not stated; it was legally no longer in effect from 2/20/26.
